S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
examples: Continually procrastinates or is reluctant to start writing long reports or complex homework.
Avoids activities that require long periods of concentration, such as reading books or studying.
Passes off tasks that require complex thinking or planning to others.
Gets annoyed or resists when asked to start a task that requires significant mental effort.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
examples: Talks incessantly and cannot tolerate silence, continuing to chatter.
Continues to talk even when others are bored or try to cut the conversation short.
Talks too much inappropriately for the situation, making people around them uncomfortable.
Monopolizes the conversation and gives almost no chance for others to speak.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Inattentive Presentation, is characterized by a persistent pattern of inattention with functional impairment, while hyperactivity-impulsivity is less central though may still appear in limited ways such as excessive talking. In adults and older adolescents it often becomes clinically apparent when external structure decreases or responsibilities increase, with disorganization, careless errors, avoidance of sustained mental effort, distractibility, and forgetfulness affecting school, work, or daily obligations. It is distinguished from ordinary stress, anxiety, or low motivation by its persistence across time and settings and by impairment that is not better explained by another condition.

patient.stressor: After finishing his bachelor’s degree, Aamer moved from his family home in New Jersey to a small apartment near Boston to pursue museum studies and independent curatorial work, losing the family routines that had quietly kept his days structured. Over the next 1 year and 11 months, the demands of managing rent, appointments, applications, research drafts, travel plans, and solitary projects exposed a pattern of missed details, disorganized task planning, avoidance of long written assignments, distraction during reading, and forgotten errands, while his tendency to talk at length in seminars and gallery discussions began to stand out. The impairment remained mild but clinically meaningful: he completed some work late, missed a few professional opportunities, and felt his careful self-image no longer matched his daily functioning. He eventually sought psychiatric evaluation through his university counseling referral network after a faculty mentor noted that his ideas were strong but his execution had become persistently unreliable.

S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
S001.manifestation: What finally made me come in is that I keep turning in applications or research notes with small but embarrassing mistakes, like a mislabeled artwork date or a skipped question, even when I honestly thought I had checked them.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
S005.manifestation: My apartment and laptop both look like half-started projects—rent papers, gallery notes, article PDFs, and to-do lists everywhere—and I have a hard time figuring out what actually needs to happen first.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
S006.manifestation: If I know a task will take real concentration, like drafting a curatorial proposal or reading a dense theory chapter, I’ll put it off with smaller errands until it’s suddenly the night before it’s due.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
S008.manifestation: When I’m trying to read or write at my desk, a siren outside, someone talking in the hallway, or even a random thought about an exhibit idea can pull me away for twenty minutes before I notice.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
S009.manifestation: I’ll mean to do normal adult things like return an email, pay a bill, or pick up groceries, and then days later I realize I never did it because it just dropped out of my mind.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
S015.manifestation: In seminars or gallery conversations I sometimes get excited and explain an idea for too long, then realize afterward that I barely left space for anyone else to respond.

add_requirements.Onset prior to age 12 years: Even in elementary school, my teachers would write that I had good ideas but forgot to turn in worksheets, lost instructions, or missed little details unless my parents checked my backpack every night.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because of this, I’ve submitted work late, missed a couple of application deadlines, and had a mentor tell me my follow-through is starting to hurt opportunities I should be ready for.
add_requirements.duration: This has been noticeable since I moved to Boston after finishing my bachelor’s, so it’s been going on for about 1 year and 11 months.
